title: Engineering All-Hands - 2026-06-03
content:
Attendees: Avery Chen (host), Samir Patel, Riley Martinez, Jordan Lee, Priya Kapoor, + ~40 engineers on stream.

Agenda:
- Quick metrics snapshot (SLOs)
- Major incidents and follow-ups
- Cross-team highlights (Serving Runtime, Platform, Private)
- Upcoming launches and freeze windows
- Open blockers and requests for help
- Action items + next steps

1) Metrics snapshot (Riley)
- P50 latency: 22ms (stable)
- P95 latency: 86ms (up 5ms w/ new batching config on canary)
- P99 latency: 260ms (still within target for hosted API 300ms)
- Token throughput: 1.9M tokens/min across hosted fleet (up 7% WoW)
- Error rate: 0.12% (spike related to edge cache ttl change on 2026-06-02)
- Cost/unit: estimated $0.00095 per token-equivalent (platform optimize work ongoing)
Notes: need to watch P95 drift on longer sequences during peak hours; investigating kernel selection heuristics.

2) Incidents & postmortems (Samir)
- 2026-06-02 11:40 UTC - edge cache TTL misconfiguration caused increased origin calls for ~18 min. Impact: minor latency spikes, few 429s due to burst.
  - Root cause: deployment applied default TTL override flag in config.
  - Remediation: roll back TTL override; reverted in 10 min.
  - Follow-up: config validation check to block overrides without explicit owner approval (PR open: github.com/.../pr/4567).
- Action: Jordan to draft postmortem for ops channel (due 2026-06-06).

3) Serving Runtime updates (Jordan)
- Canary of continuous-batching improvements is live on 5% traffic. Observed 9% cost reduction for short prompts, slight p95 increase for long prompts.
- Kernel selection: landed heuristics for small-batch kernels; still need tests for sequence len >2048.
- KV cache eviction tuning: landed on canary, memory regression on older GPUs discovered; working on fix.
- Request: more production traces from dedicated pools to validate fallback logic; product team to provide sample traffic (Priya).

4) Platform & Dedicated (Priya)
- Dedicated capacity beta: three customers onboarded, throughput targets mostly met. One customer saw queueing during daily backup window; autoscaler policy tweak pushed.
- Private (VPC) deployments: validation harness for KMS integration is ~70% complete. Expect private deployment alpha for legal team next week.
- Console: route-level latency dashboard now shows token-level cost; feedback: product wants UI drill-down to trace ids.

5) Observability / SRE (Samir)
- Traces: added new span for kernel selection decision; rollout across services next sprint.
- Alerts: threshold for 429 rate lowered from 0.5% to 0.25% for more proactive paging.
- Playbook: updated rollback steps for canary jobs (link in linked_artifacts).

6) Product / Roadmap highlights (Avery)
- Hosted API: will support structured tool-calling beta next month; internal SDKs updated.
- Optimize: first pass of quantization recommendations engine shipped to staging. Looking for 2-3 internal teams to run audits and provide prompts for quality checks.
- Rollout plan: model variant fallback feature targeted for 2026-06-20 release; freeze window scheduled 2026-06-18..2026-06-21.

7) Open blockers / asks
- Need clearer success criteria for continuous-batching canary (Jordan). Suggested: cost delta >5% and p95 within +10ms.
- Dedicated customers requesting per-tenant cache isolation docs. Platform docs owner? (Priya to assign).
- SRE asks serving-runtime to add more verbose logs for memory allocation failures (Samir).

8) Action items (short list)
- Jordan Lee - Draft incident postmortem for 2026-06-02 edge-cache TTL (due 2026-06-06).
- Priya Kapoor - Assign owner for dedicated per-tenant cache isolation docs & start draft (due 2026-06-10).
- Riley Martinez - Run extended p95 test for canary with sequences >2048 and report (due 2026-06-08).
- Samir Patel - Update SRE playbook and add rollback checklist to confluence (due 2026-06-07).
- Avery Chen - Schedule cross-team QA for model variant fallback feature (meeting invite by 2026-06-05).

Notes to self / follow-ups: 
- Track whether continuous-batching cost wins persist after kernel selection tweaks.
- Consider short-term guardrail: auto-scale down batch size if p95 > +12ms compared to baseline.
- Collect examples of failure modes from dedicated beta customers to feed into Optimize recommendations.

Misc / shoutouts:
- Thanks to infra team (Kate & team) for emergency rollback assistance on 6/2.
- Congrats to Serving Runtime on 9% cost reduction experiment (early wins).

Next all-hands: 2026-06-10 (weekly). Please add items to the confluence agenda page or ping Avery.

End of notes.
